parts.text: That leaves some people trying to manage stronger feelings of hunger at a time when their bodies need fewer

. It helps explain why keeping weight off can be difficult even when someone is still making a deliberate effort.

2. Genes influence appetite

Some of the differences in body weight between people come from the genes they
. In rare cases, a change in a single gene can cause severe obesity in early childhood. More often, many genetic differences each

a little. Studies of both patterns point to the parts of the brain involved in appetite, which helps explain why some people may feel full sooner than others.

In a Norwegian study, researchers used DNA to group people by their inherited tendency to have a higher body mass
, or BMI, a measure of weight relative to height. Over several decades,

BMI rose across the groups, with a bigger rise among those with the strongest genetic tendency.

The rise across groups points to changes in the conditions people lived in. The bigger rise in some groups suggests that the same changes can affect people differently.

3. Sleeping less can make you eat more

A review of
found that people tended to eat more when their sleep was cut short. There was much less evidence that cutting sleep changed how many calories they

.

Researchers then tested what happened when people who usually slept less than six and a half hours a night got more sleep. In a two-week trial of 80 adults with overweight, one group received advice tailored to their sleep habits and the other kept its usual

.

Those given advice slept about an hour longer and took in about 270 fewer calories a day, on average, compared with the other group. Both groups were free to choose what they ate. Whether the difference in calorie

lasts is still unclear, and keeping regular sleep hours can be difficult for people who work nights or care for someone.

4. Semaglutide can lower the risk of serious heart problems and stroke

Semaglutide
GLP-1, a hormone that helps regulate appetite. The medicine can help people feel fuller and less hungry.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: New research explores a way to repair heart tissue damaged by a heart attack.
Evidence about fluoride helps explain the differences between natural and conventional toothpaste.
Body weight reflects interacting biological, social and environmental influences.
Food-based healthcare approaches have a long history and are attracting renewed interest.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: In my new book, Obesity: Life Beyond the GLP-1 Injection, I look at what shapes body weight and what that means for treatment and prevention.

questions.prompt: What did one study find after adults lost weight on a very low-calorie diet?
options: They permanently lost the biological capacity to feel hunger.
The study showed weight depends only on individual willpower.
Their appetite disappeared in every setting.
They still reported increased hunger a year after the diet ended.
questions.explanation: 第 4 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: In one study, adults who lost weight on a very low-calorie diet still reported feeling hungrier a year after the diet ended than they had before it began.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 9?
options: A review of experiments found that people tended to eat more when their sleep was cut short.
A review of studies found that energy use can sometimes fall even further than you’d expect for a person’s new weight.
About 17 in every 100 people taking semaglutide stopped because of side effects, compared with eight in every 100 taking the placebo.
In a Norwegian study, researchers used DNA to group people by their inherited tendency to have a higher body mass index, or BMI, a measure of weight relative to height.
questions.explanation: 定位第 9 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: In a Norwegian study, researchers used DNA to group people by their inherited tendency to have a higher body mass index, or BMI, a measure of weight relative to height.
